content: Doxycycline monohydrate capsules should be used to treat or prevent infections caused by bacteria that are proven or strongly suspected to be susceptible to this antibiotic. When available, culture and susceptibility data should guide the selection or modification of therapy. In the absence of such data, local epidemiological trends and susceptibility patterns may inform empiric treatment decisions. Doxycycline is specifically indicated for the treatment of the following infections: 1. Rickettsial Infections: Rocky Mountain spotted fever Typhus fever and other typhus group infections Q fever Rickettsialpox Tick fevers caused by Rickettsiae 2. Respiratory Tract Infections: Infections caused by Mycoplasma pneumoniae 3. Chlamydial Infections: Lymphogranuloma venereum caused by Chlamydia trachomatis Psittacosis (ornithosis) caused by Chlamydia psittaci Trachoma caused by Chlamydia trachomatis (though the infectious agent may not always be completely eradicated as determined by immunofluorescence) Inclusion conjunctivitis caused by Chlamydia trachomatis Uncomplicated urethral, endocervical, or rectal infections in adults caused by Chlamydia trachomatis 4. Ureaplasma Infections: Nongonococcal urethritis caused by Ureaplasma urealyticum 5. Borrelia Infections: Relapsing fever caused by Borrelia recurrentis Doxycycline is also effective against infections caused by certain gram-negative microorganisms: 1. Haemophilus ducreyi: Chancroid 2. Yersinia pestis: Plague (formerly classified as Pasteurella pestis) 3. Francisella tularensis: Tularemia (formerly classified as Pasteurella tularensis) 4. Vibrio cholerae: Cholera (formerly classified as Vibrio comma) 5. Campylobacter fetus: Infections caused by Campylobacter fetus (formerly classified as Vibrio fetus) 6. Brucella species: Brucellosis (in combination with streptomycin) 7. Bartonella bacilliformis: Bartonellosis 8. Calymmatobacterium granulomatis: Granuloma inguinale For certain gram-negative microorganisms, doxycycline is indicated when susceptibility testing confirms its effectiveness. These include: Escherichia coli Enterobacter aerogenes (formerly Aerobacter aerogenes) Shigella species Acinetobacter species (formerly Mima and Herellea species) Respiratory tract infections caused by Haemophilus influenzae Respiratory and urinary tract infections caused by Klebsiella species Doxycycline is also indicated for infections caused by specific gram-positive microorganisms when susceptibility testing confirms its appropriateness: 1. Streptococcus pneumoniae: Upper respiratory tract infections (formerly classified as Diplococcus pneumoniae) 2. Staphylococcus aureus: Skin and skin structure infections 3. Bacillus anthracis: When penicillin is contraindicated, doxycycline serves as an alternative treatment for the following infections: Uncomplicated gonorrhea caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae Syphilis caused by Treponema pallidum Yaws caused by Treponema pertenue Listeriosis caused by Listeria monocytogenes Vincent’s infection caused by Fusobacterium fusiforme Actinomycosis caused by Actinomyces israelii Infections caused by Clostridium species In cases of acute intestinal amebiasis, doxycycline may be used as an adjunct to amebicides. Additionally, it may serve as adjunctive therapy in the management of severe acne.
